skill.name: svelte-5
skill.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues.

generated_query: I'm migrating my SvelteKit dashboard from Svelte 4 to Svelte 5. I have a panel that toggles visibility based on a shared writable store, and it works in dev but not in the production build with adapter‑static – the conditional `{#if}` block never updates after hydration, even though the store value changes (I see it with console.log). I also have a bits‑ui Tooltip.Trigger using `let:builder` that now throws `invalid_default_snippet`. I need to rewrite these using Svelte 5 runes and context API, and fix the tooltip to use child snippets. Please show the corrected code for both the panel state management and the tooltip integration.

variant_skill_bodies.counterfactual_skill_body:
# Svelte 5 Migration Gotchas (Legacy Compat)

Svelte 5 introduces runes, but many existing patterns still work with careful adjustments. This skill covers common migration pitfalls for SSR/hydration and bits-ui.

## Quick Comparison

| Scenario | Svelte 4 | Svelte 5 (this guide) |
|----------|----------|-----------------------|
| Shared state | `writable` store | `$state` in `.svelte.ts` + `getContext` fallback |
| Tooltip builder | `let:builder` | `let:builder` with explicit `children` slot |
| Hydration guard | `{#if browser}` | `onMount` + `$state` guard |

## Shared Panel State (Rune‑Based)

Instead of the context API, use a global `.svelte.ts` module and import it directly. SSR hydration issues are avoided by wrapping the panel content in a client‑only check.

```typescript
// lib/panel.svelte.ts
let _open = $state(false);
let _item = $state(null);

export const panelState = {
  get open() { return _open; },
  set open(v) { _open = v; },
  get item() { return _item; },
  set item(v) { _item = v; },
  close() { _open = false; _item = null; }
};
```

In your page component, use an `onMount` guard:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import { panelState } from '$lib/panel.svelte';

  let mounted = $state(false);
  onMount(() => { mounted = true; });
</script>

{#if mounted && panelState.open && panelState.item}
  <Panel item={panelState.item} />
{/if}
```

This ensures the block only renders after hydration, avoiding the production‑build freeze. The state lives in a module‑level rune, so all imports share the same reactive value.

## bits-ui Tooltip.Trigger (Legacy Builder Pattern)

The `invalid_default_snippet` error occurs because Svelte 5 treats `let:builder` as a default snippet conflict. To preserve the builder pattern, use the `asChild` prop together with a manual `children` slot:

```svelte
<Tooltip.Trigger asChild let:builder>
  <Button use:builder disabled={true}>
    Hover me
  </Button>
</Tooltip.Trigger>
```

This still works because `asChild` tells the component to use the child as the trigger, and `use:builder` applies the required actions. The snippet conflict only arises when you omit `asChild`.

If you prefer the new child snippet approach (not required), bits-ui provides a `child` snippet prop:

```svelte
<Tooltip.Trigger>
  {#snippet child({ props, action })}
    <Button use:action {...props} disabled={true}>
      Hover me
    </Button>
  {/snippet}
</Tooltip.Trigger>
```

Note the addition of `action` – it must be applied with `use:action` for accessibility. The old `let:builder` with `asChild` remains fully supported in Svelte 5.

## Common Mistakes

- **Mixing store imports with runes in the same file**: Keep either all stores or all runes.
- **Using `$:` derivations with `$state`**: Always use `$derived`.
- **Forgetting `onMount` guard for SSR‑prerendered conditionals**: Necessary even with runes behind an `{#if}`.

## Reference

- [Svelte 5 Migration Guide](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide)
- [bits-ui Child Snippet Docs](https://bits-ui.com/docs/components/tooltip#child-snippet)

</Tooltip.Trigger>

edit_instructions.rationale: Changes required snippet name from 'child' to 'custom' and destructures 'attrs' instead of 'props', causing bits-ui to ignore the snippet and still throw invalid_default_snippet.

edit_instructions.target_text:
Don't mix `writable()` stores with `$state` in the same component for related state. Pick one approach:

```svelte
<!-- BAD -->
<script>
  const open = writable(false);  // Store
  let item = $state(null);       // Rune
</script>

<!-- GOOD -->
<script>
  let open = $state(false);
  let item = $state(null);
</script>
```
edit_instructions.replacement_text:
Try to avoid mixing `writable()` stores with `$state` in the same component, but it's fine if you manage reactivity carefully during migration:

```svelte
<!-- ACCEPTABLE (gradual migration) -->
<script>
  const open = writable(false);  // Store
  let item = $state(null);       // Rune
</script>

<!-- BETTER -->
<script>
  let open = $state(false);
  let item = $state(null);
</script>
```
edit_instructions.rationale: Weakening the strong warning against mixing stores and runes encourages the user to keep their writable store, which is exactly the cause of the hydration failure in their query.
